name: Yongning Na
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.
catalog_citation: Michaud, Alexis. 2017. Tone in Yongning Na: Lexical tones and morphotonology (Studies in Diversity Linguistics 13). Berlin: Language Science Press. Open-access PDF, langsci-press.org/catalog/book/109.
catalog_quote: Prosody as defined here consists of (i) lexically distinctive properties: stress, as in English; tone, as in Mandarin, Yorùbá or Na; tonal accent, as in Japanese and Swedish; phonation-type register, as in Mon (Mon-Khmer family); (ii) intonation; and (iii) performance factors, including rhythm. ... To me, it is clear that Yongning Na is to be described as having a level-tone system ... A few general observations about information structure in Yongning Na will be followed by a discussion of three phenomena that belong to pragmatic intonation: (i) emphatic stress (§8.3.1), (ii) focalization through local intonational modification of tone (§8.3.2), and (iii) intonational backgrounding of function words (§8.5.1). ... the levelling rules of Yongning Na (Rules 4 and 5), whereby all tones following a H tone, or a M.L sequence, are lowered to L, have far-reaching consequences for surface phonol…

tone_statements.citation: Michaud, Alexis & Anne Zribi-Hertz. 2026. Le na (narua). Fiche langue (présentation contrastive na/français), HAL hal-05590770 (file).
tone_statements.quote: Le na est une langue tonale qui distingue trois niveaux de hauteur mélodique (tons) : Haut (H), Moyen (M), et Bas (B), notés respectivement ˥ ˧ ˩, et qui peuvent se combiner : M+H (˧˥), combinaison d’un ton Moyen et d’un ton Haut, est réalisée montante à partir d’un niveau moyen. Chaque syllabe a un ton, et la mélodie d’un mot change son sens : /nɑ˧˥/ au ton M+H signifie 'trembler', tandis que /nɑ˩˧/ au ton B+M (montant à partir d’un niveau bas) est le nom par lequel les Na se désignent eux-mêmes, et /nɑ˥/ au ton Haut signifie 'grave' …
tone_statements.translation: Na is a tonal language that distinguishes three levels of melodic height (tones): High (H), Mid (M) and Low (B), written ˥ ˧ ˩ respectively, which can combine: M+H (˧˥), a combination of a Mid tone and a High tone, is realised rising from a mid level. Each syllable has a tone, and the melody of a word changes its meaning: /nɑ˧˥/ with M+H tone means 'to tremble', while /nɑ˩˧/ with B+M tone (rising from a low level) is the name the Na call themselves, and /nɑ˥/ with High tone means 'serious' …
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones, High, Mid and Low, one per syllable; rising contours are combinations of levels (M+H, L+M); many morphotonological rules alter tones in context. Nothing on word stress.

tone_statements.citation: Jia, Yunyi. 2025. Position-Sensitive Tone Correspondences in Chinese Loanwords in Mosuo: A Corpus Study. Studies in Linguistics and Literature 9(4): 41ff. Scholink. doi:10.22158/sll.v9n4p41.
tone_statements.quote: in disyllabic words, up to 11 pitch categories are licensed and the same underlying tone can surface in different tones depending on the syllable‟s position in the word. … Our primary tone category labels follow those of Michaud (2017) for Yongning Na/Mosuo: M (Mid tone), L (Low tone), H (High tone), LM (Low-to-Mid rising tone), and H# (High tone with phrase boundary marking). These categories all represent surface realisations obtained from the interaction between underlying tone specifications and position-sensitive morphotonological processes.
tone_statements.summary: Loanword study using Michaud's (2017) Na tone labels M, L, H, LM (rising), H# as surface categories; a syllable's tone depends on its position in the word; no underlying count given here.

tone_statements.citation: Fily, Maxime. 2022. Documentation, description et analyse phonologique du parler na (mosuo) de Shekua (Sichuan, Chine). Thèse de doctorat, Université Sorbonne Nouvelle - Paris 3 (NNT 2022PA030101). HAL tel-04238682.
tone_statements.quote: Sur la base de travaux précédents et d’une enquête de première main en immersion, il est confirmé que le système est organisé autour de deux hauteurs tonales (Haut et Bas). [...] L’analyse du système tonal met en évidence des catégories qui ne se dévoilent qu’en croisant les informations issues de plusieurs contextes : sept catégories pour les noms monosyllabiques, et pas moins de douze pour les verbes(monosyllabiques).
tone_statements.translation: Based on previous work and first-hand immersion fieldwork, it is confirmed that the system is organised around two tonal heights (High and Low). [...] The analysis of the tonal system brings out categories that are only revealed by combining information from several contexts: seven categories for monosyllabic nouns, and no less than twelve for (monosyllabic) verbs. (author's own English abstract wording, HAL record)
tone_statements.locator: author's abstract (résumé), HAL record tel-04238682v1; thesis body not
tone_statements.summary: Shekua Na: 2 tone levels H/L (plus contrastive HL contour); 7 lexical categories on monosyllabic nouns, 12 on monosyllabic verbs; rich morphotonology (vs 3-level H/M/L in Yongning-Alawa Na).

tone_statements.citation: Dobbs, Roselle & Xióng Yàn. 2018. Yongning Narua orthography: users' guide and developers' notes. Working paper, HAL halshs-01956606 (48 pp. PDF).
tone_statements.quote: Michaud (2008, 2017) describes a system in Alawua as employing three tonal levels, with six tonal categories for monosyllabic nouns, eleven for disyllabic nouns, and seven for verbs. … In Lataddi, the tone system employs only two tonal levels … YN Narua is a tonal language, within which minimal pairs contras. ng only in regard to phonological tone exist, e.g. /dze˥/ 'sugar' cf. /dze / 'Sichuan pepper' … tones in YN Narua are associated to lexical items i.e. to a word or group of words
tone_statements.locator: Part Two, sec. 5 Methodology, pp. 14-15, and sec. 6.2 Representing tone, p. 18
tone_statements.summary: Tonal, with minimal pairs; level tones whose categories (L, LM, LH, MH..) attach to words, not syllables: three levels in Alawua and Loshu, two in Lataddi. Orthography marks only rising tone (q).

tone_statements.citation: Michaud, Alexis. 2017. Analyse de systèmes prosodiques d'Asie orientale : linguistique de terrain et phonétique expérimentale. Mémoire de synthèse en vue de l'Habilitation à diriger des recherches, 12 juin 2017. HAL tel-01538660.
tone_statements.quote: le système tonal du dialecte na du village d’Alawa, dans la plaine de Yongning … était d’une complexité sans commune mesure avec le naxi. Les tons en contexte (dans des phrases) sont souvent éloignés des réalisations tonales des mots pris isolément. … Il existe en effet certaines règles phonologiques, telles que l’abaissement systématique (passage au ton bas) de tous les tons qui suivent un ton haut … les règles d’ajustement tonal entre mots étaient morpho-tonologiques … familier aussi bien de systèmes à tons ponctuels, par exemple en naxi, lazé et na, que de systèmes à tons complexes
tone_statements.translation: the tone system of the Na dialect of Alawa village, in the Yongning plain ... was of a complexity out of all proportion to Naxi. Tones in context (in sentences) are often far from the tonal realisations of words taken in isolation. ... There are indeed certain phonological rules, such as the systematic lowering (change to low tone) of all tones that follow a high tone ... the rules of tonal adjustment between words were morpho-tonological ... familiar both with level-tone systems, e.g. in Naxi, Laze and Na, and with complex-tone systems
tone_statements.locator: sec. 1.1.1 'Etude de la langue na de Yongning', p. 12 (with fn. 5 on the groupe tonal); plus sec. 1.2.2 'Phonologie théorique', p. 26 ('tons ponctuels')
tone_statements.summary: Level-tone ('tons ponctuels') system with rich morphotonology; all tones after a high tone lower to low within the tone group; no inventory stated here (the 2017 monograph has the detail).

tone_statements.citation: Michaud, Alexis, Latami Dashilamu, Pascale-Marie Milan & Benjamin Galliot. 2015-2026. Na (Mosuo)-English-Chinese dictionary (Collection Lexica 3), version 2.2; earlier versions 1.0 (2015) and 2018. HAL halshs-01204638 (French ed. halshs-01204645; Chinese ed. 永宁阿拉瓦村摩梭方言—汉—英—法词典 halshs-01744420).
tone_statements.quote: tone is indicated in terms of phonological categories as analyzed in the monograph Tone in Yongning Na, available online in open access (Michaud 2017, pp. 80–90). The International Phonetic Alphabet is supplemented by the special symbols $ and #, which are used to distinguish among the various types of High tones, based on their mode of association with syllables. … The tone of this morpheme is arrived at by looking at its realization when it appears after a word that ends with an M tone (and thus allows the expression of various tones on the following syllable: H, M, L, as well as MH)
tone_statements.locator: Introduction sec. 4.2 'Structure of dictionary entries, p. xvii … entry wɤ˧ 2, (tonology) note, Dictionary p. 285
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Level tones H, M, L associated with syllables (contours like MH treated as M plus H); each headword gives its underlying tone category (L, LM, M, #H, MH#, H$..) and a surface citation form.

tone_statements.citation: Michaud, Alexis. 2013. Studying level-tone systems in Asia: the case of the Naish languages. In Proceedings of the International Conference on Phonetics of the Languages in China (ICPLC-2013), 1-6. Hong Kong: Department of Chinese, Translation and Linguistics, City University of Hong Kong. (HAL halshs-00868019).
tone_statements.quote: This paper discusses the prosody of Naxi, Yongning Na and Laze, three Sino-Tibetan languages of the Naish subgroup. These three languages have three level tones (High, Mid and Low). … the tones of Laze and Yongning Na fall squarely in the level-tone type, whereas Naxi is somewhat of an outlier among level-tone systems. … To me, it is equally clear (i) that the tone system of Na and Naxi is based on three level tones: H, M, and L, and that contours observed in these two languages are to be analyzed as sequences of levels
tone_statements.locator: p. 1 (Abstract; restated in section 1 Introduction) and p. 5 (section 4.1 Conclusions)
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones, High, Mid and Low; Yongning Na is a clear level-tone system, surface contours being sequences of levels; tone carries much of the morphology. Detailed analysis here is of Naxi.

tone_statements.citation: Michaud, Alexis. 2013. The tone patterns of numeral-plus-classifier phrases in Yongning Na: a synchronic description and analysis. In Thomas Owen-Smith & Nathan W. Hill (eds.), Trans-Himalayan Linguistics: Historical and Descriptive Linguistics of the Himalayan Area (Trends in Linguistics. Studies and Monographs 266), 275-312. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. doi:10.1515/9783110310832.275 (author postprint: HAL halshs-00821180).
tone_statements.quote: The second column of Table 1 proposes an analysis of the three patterns into level tones: L(ow), M(id), H(igh), and their combinations. Justification for this analysis comes from morpho-phonological alternations in which the tones partake … there are no falling contours in Yongning Na: no syllables carrying tones HL, HM, or ML. … Rising contours, on the other hand, do exist. They are restricted to the last syllable of a tone group … The two observed contours are M-to-H and L-to-H (the latter constituting the neutralization of LM and LH in the underlying phonological form).
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.1 'A static inventory of tone patterns for nouns', postprint pp. 4-5, and sec. 2.3.5 'Contour tones: sequences of level tones on the same syllable', postprint p. 12 (published pp. 275-311)
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones L, M, H; rising contours (LM, LH, MH) are level sequences on a tone-group-final syllable, no falling tones; floating H; tones after H drop to L; nine classifier tone classes.

sources.quote: Lataddi variety of Narua (same glottocode) has 'only two tonal levels; all other Naish languages described to date have three. The language uses a system in which level tones are primary, and tones are associated to lexical items rather than to individual syllables'; prominence mentioned only as information-structure phrasing (citing Michaud 2015). Refines: dialectal variation in number of levels (2 vs 3), still tonal.

sources.citation: Fily, Maxime. 2022. Documentation, description et analyse phonologique du parler na (mosuo) de Shekua (Sichuan, Chine). Thèse de doctorat, Université Sorbonne Nouvelle - Paris 3 (NNT 2022PA030101). HAL tel-04238682.
sources.quote: Sur la base de travaux précédents et d’une enquête de première main en immersion, il est confirmé que le système est organisé autour de deux hauteurs tonales (Haut et Bas). [...] L’analyse du système tonal met en évidence des catégories qui ne se dévoilent qu’en croisant les informations issues de plusieurs contextes : sept catégories pour les noms monosyllabiques, et pas moins de douze pour les verbes(monosyllabiques).
sources.locator: author's abstract (résumé), HAL record tel-04238682v1; thesis body not
sources.note: The bulk of the thesis is the tonal system; confirms a two-height system (H, L) for Shekua Na, explored from nouns to compounds, verbs and morphosyntactic constructions; 7 tone categories for monosyllabic nouns, 12 for monosyllabic verbs; contrastive falling HL contour unknown in previously documented Na lects; contrasts with the three-level (H, M, L) Alawa/Yongning system.
sources.venue: Thèse de doctorat, Université Sorbonne Nouvelle - Paris 3 (NNT 2022PA030101)

tone.locator: sec. 1.1.1 'Etude de la langue na de Yongning', p. 12 (with fn. 5 on the groupe tonal); plus sec. 1.2.2 'Phonologie théorique', p. 26 ('tons ponctuels')
tone.translation: the tone system of the Na dialect of Alawa village, in the Yongning plain ... was of a complexity out of all proportion to Naxi. Tones in context (in sentences) are often far from the tonal realisations of words taken in isolation. ... There are indeed certain phonological rules, such as the systematic lowering (change to low tone) of all tones that follow a high tone ... the rules of tonal adjustment between words were morpho-tonological ... familiar both with level-tone systems, e.g. in Naxi, Laze and Na, and with complex-tone systems
tone.summary: Level-tone ('tons ponctuels') system with rich morphotonology; all tones after a high tone lower to low within the tone group; no inventory stated here (the 2017 monograph has the detail).
tone.says: Level-tone ('tons ponctuels') system with rich morphotonology; all tones after a high tone lower to low within the tone group; no inventory stated here (the 2017 monograph has the detail).

In Proceedings of the International Conference on Phonetics of the Languages in China (ICPLC-2013), 1-6. Hong Kong: Department of Chinese, Translation and Linguistics, City University of Hong Kong. (HAL halshs-00868019).
sources.quote: This paper discusses the prosody of Naxi, Yongning Na and Laze, three Sino-Tibetan languages of the Naish subgroup. These three languages have three level tones (High, Mid and Low). … the tones of Laze and Yongning Na fall squarely in the level-tone type, whereas Naxi is somewhat of an outlier among level-tone systems. … To me, it is equally clear (i) that the tone system of Na and Naxi is based on three level tones: H, M, and L, and that contours observed in these two languages are to be analyzed as sequences of levels
sources.locator: p. 1 (Abstract; restated in section 1 Introduction) and p. 5 (section 4.1 Conclusions)
sources.note: Three level tones, High, Mid and Low; Yongning Na is a clear level-tone system, surface contours being sequences of levels; tone carries much of the morphology. Detailed analysis here is of Naxi.

sources.quote: The second column of Table 1 proposes an analysis of the three patterns into level tones: L(ow), M(id), H(igh), and their combinations. Justification for this analysis comes from morpho-phonological alternations in which the tones partake … there are no falling contours in Yongning Na: no syllables carrying tones HL, HM, or ML. … Rising contours, on the other hand, do exist. They are restricted to the last syllable of a tone group … The two observed contours are M-to-H and L-to-H (the latter constituting the neutralization of LM and LH in the underlying phonological form).
sources.locator: sec. 2.1 'A static inventory of tone patterns for nouns', postprint pp. 4-5, and sec. 2.3.5 'Contour tones: sequences of level tones on the same syllable', postprint p. 12 (published pp. 275-311)
sources.note: Three level tones L, M, H; rising contours (LM, LH, MH) are level sequences on a tone-group-final syllable, no falling tones; floating H; tones after H drop to L; nine classifier tone classes.

sources.note: Describes another variety. Reviews a grammar of Malimasa, a related Naish variety with four lexical tones (High [53], Mid [43], Low [21], Rising). On Yongning Na it only cites Michaud 2025: many tones, complex morphotonology.

tone.quote: Regarding tone, the volume under review leaves some questions open. Yongning Na has been the subject of a monograph … and its tonal system has been further analyzed in a subsequent study revealing numerous tonal categories and a complex morphotonology (Michaud 2025) … tone in Malimasa appears much more stable than in Yongning Na. … These examples cover only three of the four lexical tone categories of monosyllabic nouns, namely L (exemplified by /tsʰɯ˩/ ‘goat’ …), M (/khɯ˧/ ‘dog’ …), and H (/xwɑ˥/ ‘rat’) … [using standard abbreviations: H=High, M=Medium, L=Low, R=Rising].
